subject: Contingency & cutover window for billing vendor consolidation
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Contingency & cutover window for billing vendor consolidation

Hi Laura / Tessa —

Quick summary: procurement asked for a contingency plan in case BillMate refuses our proposed SLA changes or pricing. We also need a firm cutover window for any migration to NetSuite billing connectors so we can schedule Eng and Finance outages.

Attachments: vendor_shortlist_v2.xlsx, migration_risks.md (first pass).

Asking for:
- Laura: a procurement timeline with legal lead times for a 30/60/90-day extension (if needed).
- Tessa: high-level engineering work estimate for a staged cutover (prefix caching, invoice backfill, webhook reconciliation).
- Dylan: an ops fallback checklist (what to disable if sync errors spike).

Goal: make a recommendation to leadership by 11/14 so we can lock the Q4 budget.

thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Finance & Ops Partner
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Contingency & cutover window for billing vendor consolidation

On Thu, Oct 28, 2026 at 9:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick summary: procurement asked for a contingency plan...

Thanks Marcus — attaching a draft procurement timeline (procurement_timeline_2026Q4.pdf). Key notes:
- We can negotiate a 60-day extension with BillMate with minimal legal changes (standard SLA addendum).
- Anything beyond 90 days triggers a full SOW + SOC 2 evidence refresh (30–45 day legal review).
- If we switch to NetSuite billing connector, we should plan for a 6-week pilot with a small customer subset before full cutover.

Open items:
1) Pricing: BillMate's last offer was +8% on tokenized invoice volumes. We should push for an annual commitment discount or temporary rate cap during migration.
2) Termination liabilities: if we port invoice history, we need to confirm export format and retention windows.

I propose we run two parallel tracks: negotiate short extension while finalizing NetSuite POC. I'll loop Legal if you want me to start redlines.

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference
From: Spenser Holt <spenser@billmate.io>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: olivia.procure@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-11-09T11:48:00-08:00
Subject: BillMate — Final RFP response and commercial proposal

Marcus —

Thanks for the time last week. Attached is our final RFP response (BillMate_Final_RFP_response.pdf) plus the SLA redlines we discussed (BillMate_SLA_redlines.docx). Highlights:
- 99.95% uptime SLA, credits up to 20% for sustained outages > 1 hour.
- 45-day data retention export guarantee with S3 transfer option.
- Migration assistance: 40 hours of engineering support included for invoice export/import helpers.

If you need a tighter migration SLA or additional engineering hours, we can quote that but it will affect the commercial.

Let me know which items are blockers and we'll try to accommodate.

Best,
Spenser Holt
Director, Strategic Accounts
BillMate Inc.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Spenser Holt <spenser@billmate.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-12T08:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BillMate — Final RFP response and commercial proposal

Spenser — thanks for the packet. A couple quick clarifications before we escalate to commercial leadership:

1) The 40 hours of migration assistance — is that remote only or can you provide a brief onsite/warroom at our SF office for the cutover? We anticipate two 4-hour high-risk windows; onsite would be a plus.
2) Data export format — will the export be a single NDJSON per invoice with line-level KPIs and tax events? We need to ingest into our NetSuite staging tables without manual transforms.
3) Can BillMate commit to a 30-day rate cap if we agree to a 60-day extension? That buys us runway for the POC.

Laura / Tessa / Dylan — please respond inline with constraints/costs so I can consolidate.

Cheers,
Marcus
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-14T17:40:00-08:00
Subject: Decision: 60-day extension + NetSuite POC (recommended)

Team — after reviewing proposals and legal exposure, procurement recommends the following path:

1) Sign a 60-day extension with BillMate with the following must-haves: 30-day rate cap, included remote migration support elevated to 60 hours, and delivery of invoice export in NDJSON with schema.
2) Execute NetSuite connector POC in parallel (6-week window) using a pilot tenant and a 10-customer sample to validate backfill and webhook reconciliation.
3) Contingency: if BillMate fails to deliver NDJSON export within 10 business days of extension, trigger scheduled cutover to a read-only mode and accelerate NetSuite import.

I'll prepare redlines and a short procurement addendum for signatures. We should brief Finance leadership tomorrow morning (11/15 09:30 PT) and confirm budget reallocation for migration engineering hours.

Attachments: procurement_timeline_2026Q4.pdf (updated).

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference
